newsitem.title: GERMANY: German farm futures to start in mid-November.
newsitem.headline: German farm futures to start in mid-November.

text.p: Germany's farm futures exchange in Hanover will start electronic dealings in mid-November, Friedrich Rode, chairman of holding company Warenterminboerse (WTB) AG, said on Thursday.
"We're building up the exchange and, barring anything unforeseen, it will start working in November," he told a grain seminar.
Mark-based live pig futures would be the first contract, followed by wheat.
Guenther Wudy of the exchange's supervisory committee said a potato contract might start up in February 1998.
Wudy, of Frankfurt-based Commerzbank, also said options should be introduced six months after the exchange's start-up.
Rode was optimistic about interest not only from the domestic market but also from the Czech republic, Poland and Ukraine.

"Demand from eastern Europe is high, there will be more of a branching out in that direction than competition with existing farm futures in western Europe," he said, citing Amsterdam's ATA and Matif in Paris.
Issues still to be resolved centre on the clearing house, certain management positions and rules of membership.
Wudy said the bourse, housed in the Lower Saxony stock exchange in Hanover, should be prepared to establish non-farm contracts, especially in the critical first few years.
"The exchange probably will not survive without a range of non-farm contracts such as heating oil, gas, electricity or recycled paper," he said.
Delegates at the meeting said the pig market was more than ready to embrace the new project following this year's sharp prices rises.
Proposed malting barley and rapeseed contracts held little chance of success, they said.
